title: QueryGPT – Natural Language to SQL Using Generative AI
note: How a hackathon text-to-SQL demo became a daily tool for operations teams: curated workspaces, an intent step, a table step with a human confirmation, column pruning, then generation.

title: Running a Software Factory Efficiently at Uber Scale
note: The platform under Uber's agentic SDLC: an AI context graph, an MCP gateway over a thousand tool servers, an LLM gateway, and why an ungrounded agent fails slowly rather than cheaply.

title: Minions: Stripe's one-shot, end-to-end coding agents
note: Task-scoped agents that start from a Slack reaction or a ticket, run in isolated devboxes on a fork of Goose with hundreds of MCP tools, and open tested pull requests for human review.

title: Minions: Stripe's one-shot, end-to-end coding agents — Part 2
note: The Stripe-specific work behind the minions: blueprints that mix deterministic steps with agent loops, verification, and making a large codebase legible to agents.

title: How we engineered LinkedIn's Hiring Assistant
note: LinkedIn's first production agent: a supervisor over intake, sourcing, evaluation and outreach sub-agents, message-based orchestration, a skills registry and layered memory.

title: Engineering LinkedIn's Hiring Assistant for International Markets
note: What changed when the same AI agent had to work across languages and markets: localisation, sourcing behaviour and evaluation outside the US.

title: Building effective agents
note: The workflows-versus-agents taxonomy most teams now use: prompt chaining, routing, parallelisation, orchestrator-workers and evaluator-optimiser, with advice on when not to build an agent.

title: How we built our multi-agent research system
note: An orchestrator that spawns parallel research subagents: delegation prompts, effort scaling, tool design, evaluation with rubrics and humans, and what production required.

title: Writing tools for agents
note: How to design, describe and evaluate the tools an agent calls, including letting the model improve its own tool descriptions.

title: Effective context engineering for AI agents
note: Context as a finite attention budget: system prompt calibration, tool curation, compaction, structured note-taking and sub-agent architectures.

title: Don't Build Multi-Agents
note: Two principles from building Devin: share full context, and remember that actions carry implicit decisions, so parallel writers produce incoherent results.

title: Multi-Agents: What's Actually Working
note: A year on: swarms remain a distraction, but map-reduce-and-manage setups where extra agents contribute intelligence and writes stay single-threaded do work.

title: Context Engineering for AI Agents: Lessons from Building Manus
note: Six lessons from rebuilding an agent framework four times: design around the KV-cache, mask tools instead of removing them, use the file system as context, recite the plan, keep errors in, avoid few-shot ruts.

title: Code Mode: the better way to use MCP
note: Turn an MCP server into a typed TypeScript API and let the model write code against it inside a sandbox with bindings instead of credentials.

title: Automation Platform v2: Improving conversational AI at Airbnb
note: A hybrid customer-support platform: chain-of-thought tool use where flexibility helps, static workflows where exactness matters, plus context management, parallel guardrails and observability.

title: Integrations That Write Themselves
note: An agent that builds a missing integration for a customer in minutes, and an internal factory where a coding agent researches an API, writes the connector, tests it with real credentials and opens a pull request.
